passages.note: House final reading roll call showing his Aye; no member voted No, so the tally is near-unanimous and cannot carry a chair alone.
Bill overview names him prime sponsor of the digital-impersonation bill signed as Chapter 193.

passages.provision_quote: A provider of an interactive computer service may not be subject to an action for DIGITAL IMPERSONATION for PUBLISHING INFORMATION that is provided by another information content provider.
passages.note: The enacted section creates a private cause of action against the publisher of a deepfake and expressly exempts interactive computer services, so it sets no platform duty either way.

rows.reasoning: Kolodin prime-sponsored and voted Aye on HB2394 (2024), whose operative section creates a private suit for digital impersonation and provides that "A provider of an interactive computer service may not be subject to an action for DIGITAL IMPERSONATION for PUBLISHING INFORMATION that is provided by another information content provider." That is adjacent to the dimension these rungs separate: the bill does not "legally require platforms to remove false information", does not "require platforms to label false content, rather than remove it", does not "encourage voluntary standards for combating misinformation online", and neither prevents government censorship nor bans government involvement in content moderation. The House vote is near-unanimous besides, so it could not carry a chair even if the bill were on-question.
